classification.difficultyReason: Read endpoint changes from graph scales and calculate gradients; the hardest case also requires converting the time axis from minutes to seconds before reporting acceleration in m/s².

content.prompt: Using the graphs below, calculate the acceleration/deceleration in each case in $\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s}^2}$.

spec.description: Arrowed speed-time axes with a neutral grid and a blue straight segment. Explicit grid steps are 2 seconds horizontally and 1 m/s vertically.
spec.mathematics: Segment from (0,0) to (16,6); grid extends to 22 seconds and 8 m/s. Horizontal labels 2 to 20 by 2; vertical labels 1 to 7.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible; the numerical acceleration is answer-only.

spec.description: Arrowed speed-time axes with a neutral grid and a blue straight segment. Explicit grid steps are 2 seconds horizontally and 1 m/s vertically.
spec.mathematics: Segment from (0,2) to (15,5); grid extends to 22 seconds and 8 m/s. Horizontal labels 2 to 20 by 2; vertical labels 1 to 7. The endpoint lies halfway between the 14-second and 16-second grid lines.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible; the numerical acceleration is answer-only.

spec.description: Arrowed speed-time axes with a neutral grid and a blue straight segment. Explicit grid steps are 0.5 seconds horizontally and 5 m/s vertically.
spec.mathematics: Segment from (0,0) to (5,35); grid extends to 5.5 seconds and 40 m/s. Horizontal labels 1 to 5; vertical labels 5 to 35 by 5.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible; the numerical acceleration is answer-only.

spec.description: Arrowed speed-time axes, retaining minutes on the horizontal axis. Explicit grid steps are 1/12 minute horizontally and 10 m/s vertically.
spec.mathematics: Segment from (0,0) to (2/3,70), with time in minutes; grid extends to 13/12 minutes and 80 m/s. Horizontal labels 0.5 and 1; vertical labels 10 to 70 by 10.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible; the time conversion and acceleration are answer-only.

spec.description: Arrowed speed-time axes with a neutral grid and a blue descending straight segment. Explicit grid steps are 2 seconds horizontally and 1 m/s vertically.
spec.mathematics: Segment from (0,5) to (20,0); grid extends to 22 seconds and 8 m/s. Horizontal labels 2 to 20 by 2; vertical labels 1 to 7.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible; acceleration and deceleration values are answer-only.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}a&=\dfrac{0-5}{20-0}\\&=-0.25\ \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s}^2}\end{align*}$
The negative gradient means the speed decreases, so the deceleration is $0.25\ \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s}^2}$.

spec.description: Arrowed speed-time axes, retaining minutes on the horizontal axis. Explicit grid steps are 1/12 minute horizontally and 10 m/s vertically.
spec.mathematics: Segment from (0,60) to (1,0), with time in minutes; grid extends to 13/12 minutes and 80 m/s. Horizontal labels 0.5 and 1; vertical labels 10 to 70 by 10.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible; the conversion and acceleration/deceleration values are answer-only.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}t&=1\times60\\&=60\ \mathrm{s}\\a&=\dfrac{0-60}{60-0}\\&=-1\ \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s}^2}\end{align*}$
The negative gradient means the speed decreases, so the deceleration is $1\ \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s}^2}$.
